_comment: Shared error contract, read by python/tests/test_error_contract.py.
It exists for two measured defects:
1. SHAPE. The two servers produced different `data` for an identical
request. Python nested the tool-specific keys under `data.details`;
Node spread them flat and, in rejectUnknownArguments, attached no data
at all. A caller branching on `data.unknown` worked on Node and read
`undefined` on Python - silently, and on exactly the branch written to
handle the error. `unknown_arguments` pins the whole payload.
2. VALUE RENDERING. Python's repr writes None/True/'x' where TypeScript
writes null/true/"x". Same request, two different error strings, and an
agent that string-matches has to handle both. Both sides now render
through a shared `describe` and `handlers` pins the exact text.
Neither defect was visible to either side's own tests, because each only
ever looked at its own output. Hence a shared fixture: a per-side
assertion would restate the same bug twice.
`deliberately_not_argument_faults` records codes chosen AGAINST the grain,
so a later mechanical sweep to INVALID_ARGUMENT does not undo a decision

handlers.name: write: target_path wrong type
handlers.message: target_path must be a non-empty string, got 42.

handlers.name: write: target_path empty
handlers.message: target_path must be a non-empty string, got "".

handlers.name: write: content wrong type
handlers.message: content must be a string, got 42. Use "" to blank a script.

handlers.name: update: edits not a list
handlers.message: edits must be a non-empty list, got {}. Send [{"old_string": ..., "new_string": ...}].

handlers.name: update: edits element not an object
handlers.message: edits[1] must be an object {old_string, new_string}, got 42.

handlers.name: update: old_string wrong type
handlers.message: edits[0].old_string must be a non-empty string, got 42.

handlers.name: update: old_string empty
handlers.message: edits[0].old_string must be a non-empty string, got "".

handlers.name: update: new_string explicitly null
handlers.message: edits[0].new_string must be a string (it may be ""), got null.
handlers.why: Node used `d[key] ?? d[camelAlias]`, which treats an explicit null as absent, so this said "got undefined" where Python said "got null". null is the value a caller most needs identified.

handlers.name: skill: skill_name wrong type
handlers.message: skill_name must be a string when given, got 42. Omit it for the index of available skills.

handlers.name: manage: unknown action
handlers.message: unknown action "listt". Accepted: launch, list, make_place, places, stop.

handlers.name: manage: stop without studio_id
handlers.message: studio_id is required for action='stop'. Call action='list' with this tool - its mesh rows carry one.

handlers.name: manage: launch without place_path
handlers.message: place_path is required for action='launch'. Run action='places' or action='make_place' to choose one.

handlers.name: wait_for: condition wrong type
handlers.message: condition must be a non-empty string, got 42.

deliberately_not_argument_faults.site: writer, chunked write exhausted its retries
deliberately_not_argument_faults.message: Chunked write failed: Lua long-bracket collision persists.
deliberately_not_argument_faults.why: Our own encoder failing to escape the caller's content after five retries. The request was fine. UNKNOWN is the honest code for 'we do not know what went wrong'; INVALID_ARGUMENT would tell the caller to edit a request that did not need editing.

deliberately_not_argument_faults.message: payload head/tail mismatch; the read is not intact
deliberately_not_argument_faults.why: An integrity failure between us and Studio, not a caller fault and not an engine refusal. There is no code in the vocabulary for 'our own transport lied', and inventing one here would overstate what we know.

sites.message: line must be a 1-based positive integer, got 0.
query must be a non-empty string, got "".
max_results must be between 1 and 100, got 0.
max_results must be an integer, got "x".
context_lines must be between 0 and 10, got 11.
query is not a valid regex (regex=true): unterminated character set at position 1
sites.why: The tail is the regex engine's own wording - Python re and JS RegExp differ - passed through verbatim rather than paraphrasing an error we did not write. The code is ours and is pinned.

sites.message: className must be one of ["LocalScript","ModuleScript","Script"]; got "Part".
target_path must start with "game." (game-tree path); got "/tmp/x.lua". Use a DataModel dot-path like 'game.ServerScriptService.MyScript'.
target_path must be a game-tree path starting with "game.", got "/tmp/x.lua". File-system paths go to write_script.
edits[0].old_string not found in content. Re-read the script and copy the text exactly - matching is exact, including indentation and line endings.
edits[0].old_string matched 2 times; exactly 1 is required. Add surrounding lines to narrow it to a unique block, or set replace_all=true on this edit to replace all occurrences.
edits[0].old_string equals new_string. Send different text, or set skip_no_ops=true to drop it.
edits[0].old_string is empty. An empty old_string has no unique match; send the text to replace.
edits[0] must be an (old_string, new_string) tuple or dict, got 42.
file_path must name an existing local file, got "C:\\nope.luau". Read the path back before sending it.
sites.why: code_only because the message embeds the path _confined() resolved, and that spelling is per-machine: identical to the input on Windows, but on macOS a Windows-style argument resolves to <cwd>/C:\\nope.luau because backslashes are legal filename characters there. Pinning the literal therefore fails on exactly the platforms it was written to generalise to. The code is still pinned, by test_each_site_carries_its_declared_code. And the reason this message once mattered - a text containing 'not found' used to classify as NOT_FOUND - is now structural rather than textual: classify() returns an existing ToolError unchanged (errors.py:268), so it never reads this message at all.

sites.message: RGBA length 10 does not match 4x4x4 = 64
sites.why: Left on UNKNOWN/SIZE_LIMIT on purpose. These check our own integrity against what Studio sent, not the caller's argument. INVALID_ARGUMENT would send the caller off to edit a request that was fine. See deliberately_not_argument_faults.

sites.message: unexpected capture header: "only\ttwo\tfields"
sites.why: Left on UNKNOWN/SIZE_LIMIT on purpose. These check our own integrity against what Studio sent, not the caller's argument. INVALID_ARGUMENT would send the caller off to edit a request that was fine. See deliberately_not_argument_faults.

sites.message: capture failed in Studio: bad allocation
sites.why: Left on UNKNOWN/SIZE_LIMIT on purpose. These check our own integrity against what Studio sent, not the caller's argument. INVALID_ARGUMENT would send the caller off to edit a request that was fine. See deliberately_not_argument_faults.

sites.message: parent_path must be a game-tree path starting with "game."; got "/tmp".

captured a 2x2 PNG (68 bytes) but could not write it to "C:\\tmp\\no-such-dir\\shot.png": ENOENT. The parent directory must exist and be writable. The capture itself succeeded; the encoded PNG is discarded when this call returns and is NOT retrievable afterwards, so re-capture rather than retry the write. Either pass a save_path whose parent directory exists and is writable, or omit save_path to get png_base64 in the result - the latter has no filesystem dependency but rides this transport's return channel, which truncates at exactly 100,015 characters with no error, so it is only safe while png_bytes stays under about 75,000.
sites.why: The pixels are fine and the request is what cannot be honoured: the path the caller supplied does not name a writable file. UNKNOWN was the status quo and is classify()'s catch-all, so branching on it catches every unrelated failure; a new WRITE_FAILED code would buy no decision the errno in data does not already make, for permanent public surface in two implementations. Deliberately NOT prefixed 'capture:' - the three capture: sites are integrity checks on what Studio sent, and INVALID_ARGUMENT there would send the caller to edit a request that was fine. The one case the code overstates is ENOSPC, where the path is fine and the disk is full; data.errno says so. code_only because the message embeds a temp-dir path and an OS errno, which differ per machine and per platform.
